thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: *INC-2147* created
Severity: SEV-2 (internal dogfood)
Service: Dedicated Pools / Rollouts
Signal: queue depth + p95 latency regression
Primary: Sean Gallagher

Sean Gallagher: I’m seeing queue depth spiking on dogfood dedicated pool `dp-dogfood-07` right after staged rollout advanced to Stage 2. p95 went from ~380ms -> 2.8s, timeouts ticking up.

Allison Grant: Confirmed on dashboard. `queue_depth` is climbing steadily (currently 140+). `timeout_rate` crossed 1.2% over 5m. Linking panel: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/dedicated-pool?var-pool=dp-dogfood-07

Owen Phillips: Also seeing customer-like symptoms on our internal canary traffic. Some requests stuck ~30s then fail.

Rafael Mendes: Let’s treat as stop-the-line for dogfood. Sean, can you confirm what changed? Was this the staged rollout plan for the runtime config?

Sean Gallagher: Yep. Rollout plan `rp_9f2c` (Dedicated staged rollouts) moved from Stage 1 (5%) to Stage 2 (25%) at 17:02 PT. Gate looked “green” but traffic shift coincides exactly with queue growth.

Mina Haddad: Routing side: stage weights are enforced via deterministic hash. If we went 25% that means 25% of requests now hitting new variant in same pool. If the new variant is slower, queue will rise quickly.

Elena Popov: I can pull per-variant utilization. One sec.

Keiko Yamamoto: Any autoscaling events? Dedicated pool should be fixed capacity; but we have headroom guardrail in place. If headroom is near zero this will saturate.

Logan Wright: Checking telemetry freshness + evaluator outputs. Also want to verify metrics aren’t delayed (we’ve had lag today).

Connor O'Brien: For mitigation: can we force plan to HOLD or roll back stage weights to 0% for new variant? Need to avoid thrashing.

Sean Gallagher: First action: pausing stage advancement now. Using admin tool: `rolloutsctl pause --pool dp-dogfood-07 --plan rp_9f2c --reason "queue depth spike"`

IncidentBot: Sean Gallagher set incident status to *Investigating*

Allison Grant: Alert fired as well: `DedicatedPoolQueueDepthHigh` (threshold 80, currently 163). Paging policy is dogfood-only.

Vikram Singh: Data plane perspective: are we seeing GPU util pegged? If it’s 100% but throughput lower, could be kernel regression.

Elena Popov: GPU util for the new variant nodes is 96-99% sustained; baseline nodes ~70%. Also `tokens/s` looks ~35% lower on new variant.

Mina Haddad: That aligns with queue depth. Suggest immediate rollback to Stage 0 (0% traffic to new). Pausing alone doesn’t shift traffic back.

Rafael Mendes: Agree. Let’s explicitly set stage weights back to Stage 1 or 0. Connor/Sean, do we have a safe command?

Sean Gallagher: Yep. We can `rolloutsctl set-stage --stage stage_0` which pins routing weights to 0% for candidate.

Connor O'Brien: Do that. Also capture current rollout state for postmortem.

Sean Gallagher: Executing: `rolloutsctl set-stage --pool dp-dogfood-07 --plan rp_9f2c --stage stage_0 --reason "mitigation: rollback traffic"`

IncidentBot: Change logged: rollout rp_9f2c set to stage_0 by Sean Gallagher

Allison Grant: Watching metrics. Queue depth should start draining in 2-5 minutes if we removed the slow path.

Logan Wright: FYI evaluator “green” is based on 5m windows. If advancement happened at 17:02, it may have used pre-shift baseline. We should confirm evaluator reads post-shift windows before advancing.

Thomas Baird: Also possible we’re aggregating p95 across whole pool; at 5% stage it looked fine but at 25% p95 tail gets wrecked. Gate should likely evaluate per-variant or at least compare delta.

Keiko Yamamoto: Headroom: `available_tokens_per_sec` margin was thin (~12%). Our guardrail is currently only warning, not blocking. At 25% stage, the candidate’s lower throughput burned all headroom.

Vikram Singh: Do we know what changed in candidate? Runtime build? Quant profile?

Sean Gallagher: Candidate is `runtime-1.19.0-rc3` with the new batching defaults + gate-evaluator instrumentation. Baseline is `runtime-1.18.6`.

Elena Popov: I see candidate has `max_batch_tokens` bumped from 8192 -> 16384 and `prefill_chunking=on`. That could increase latency under this traffic shape.

Mina Haddad: If the candidate is slower, deterministic hashing will concentrate certain sessions. But at 25% we’re not skewing; it’s uniform-ish. Still enough to saturate.

Allison Grant: Update: queue depth peaked at 188 and now trending down (171 -> 154). p95 falling too (2.8s -> 1.9s). Good sign.

Rafael Mendes: Great. Keep monitoring until we’re back to normal. Once stable we’ll decide whether to fully abort plan and disable the dogfood flag.

Owen Phillips: Timeouts still at ~0.9% but dropping.

Logan Wright: Metrics latency looks ok (ingest delay ~20s). This is real, not a metrics ghost.

Connor O'Brien: For safety, can we disable automatic advancement for all dogfood pools until we understand? I don’t want other pools hitting Stage 2 tonight.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. I can flip feature flag `dedicated_staged_rollouts_auto_advance` off for dogfood tenant.

Keiko Yamamoto: Please do. Also consider reverting candidate config change (`max_batch_tokens`). But for now: stop the rollout.

Sean Gallagher: Flipping flag: `ffctl set dedicated_staged_rollouts_auto_advance --scope tenant:dogfood --value false --reason "INC-2147"`

IncidentBot: Feature flag updated by Sean Gallagher: dedicated_staged_rollouts_auto_advance -> false (tenant:dogfood)

Allison Grant: Queue depth now 92. p95 620ms. Almost back to baseline.

Rafael Mendes: Nice. Let’s mark mitigation in channel: traffic rolled back to Stage 0 + auto-advance disabled.

Mina Haddad: One more thing: did routing cache stage weights? Any propagation delay? Just to ensure we’re truly at 0%.

Elena Popov: I checked per-variant request counters: candidate QPS fell from ~220 rps to ~3 rps (health checks). Looks like traffic is effectively off.

Vikram Singh: Candidate nodes still running hot? They might be draining. But at 0% they’ll go idle.

Owen Phillips: User-facing symptoms gone for internal canary. New requests are fine.

Thomas Baird: We should capture a before/after snapshot of: tokens/s, batch sizes, queue depth, GPU util. Helps root cause whether batching default is the culprit.

Logan Wright: I can export a quick timeseries from 16:55-17:20 with the stage transition annotated.

Allison Grant: I’ll drop screenshot links in the postmortem doc later. For now metrics look stable: queue depth 41, timeout_rate 0.12%, p95 410ms.

Rafael Mendes: Decision: halt dogfood rollout plan `rp_9f2c` for now. Sean, can you abort the plan so nobody accidentally resumes it?

Sean Gallagher: Yep. `rolloutsctl abort --pool dp-dogfood-07 --plan rp_9f2c --reason "INC-2147: perf regression at Stage 2"`

IncidentBot: Change logged: rollout rp_9f2c aborted by Sean Gallagher

Connor O'Brien: Thanks. Also please note: this is the same plan template we were going to use for beta. We need a blocker fix: guardrail should prevent stage advance if projected headroom < X.

Keiko Yamamoto: +1. Our autoscaling guardrail is insufficient for Dedicated. We need a hard gate: “min headroom” computed from recent throughput + candidate perf.

Mina Haddad: From routing side we can also add a “cap candidate concurrency” so even at 25% weight it doesn’t consume full pool. But that’s more complex.

Thomas Baird: Another immediate improvement: gate evaluation should require data *after* weight change (e.g., wait 2m warmup + evaluate 5m) and compare against baseline stage.

Logan Wright: Also, evaluator currently advances based on `pool.p95_latency` and `pool.5xx_rate` but not `queue_depth` (it’s optional). In this plan we didn’t include queue depth gate. That’s on us.

Sean Gallagher: Yeah, rollout plan had only latency + 5xx. Queue depth exploded but latency gate didn’t trip fast enough.

Allison Grant: It did trip eventually but after ~7 minutes. The “gate green” at advancement time was stale window.

Rafael Mendes: Action items:
- Add queue depth as default gate for Dedicated staged rollouts.
- Ensure evaluator uses post-shift evaluation window / warmup.
- Tighten headroom guardrail to block stage advancement.
- Review candidate runtime batching default changes.
We’ll do a postmortem (lightweight) since this is dogfood but it’s exactly what we’re trying to prevent.

IncidentBot: Reminder: Postmortem required for SEV-2. Template: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/ONCALL/Postmortem+Template

Connor O'Brien: I’ll open a tracking ticket + link the incident. Sean/Rafael, who’s writing?

Rafael Mendes: Sean as primary author, I’ll review. Allison/Keiko/Mina/Logan add sections for metrics/guardrails/routing/telemetry.

Sean Gallagher: Works. I’ll start draft tonight.

Owen Phillips: Anything else to do operationally? pool looks healthy.

Allison Grant: All alerts cleared. Queue depth steady at 18. p95 ~390ms.

Rafael Mendes: Cool. We can resolve incident once we confirm for 10 more minutes.

Sean Gallagher: Monitoring… stable.

IncidentBot: Sean Gallagher set incident status to *Monitoring*

Keiko Yamamoto: Before close: can we ensure no other pool has an active plan in Stage 1/2? just to be safe.

Connor O'Brien: I ran `rolloutsctl list --tenant dogfood` earlier; only this one was active. With auto-advance disabled now, should be fine.

Logan Wright: Confirmed no evaluator advancement events since flag flip.

Sean Gallagher: Closing. Incident mitigated by rolling back traffic to baseline + aborting rollout plan. Follow-ups in postmortem.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: *INC-2147* resolved by Sean Gallagher
Resolution: aborted rollout rp_9f2c; pinned traffic off candidate; auto-advance disabled for dogfood tenant
